solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Artist performing without one is communicating via waves

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the performing word goes round the one

parts.note: performing a task is doing it
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A painter takes up performance and keeps in touch over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so I sits inside DOING.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending messages by radio is transmitting through electromagnetic waves.

clue.text: Part evidently owing was settled

indicators.note: evidently suggests plainly seen inside, so the part sits within the owing word

parts.note: in the red, owing money
a side is a part, as of an argument

explanation.surface: Someone who owes plainly lived somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lived or dwelt in a place is to have been settled there.

clue.text: Pulse of boy rising

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy's heart rate going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils and other legumes are pulses, and the Indian split-pea dish is one.

clue.text: Excluded boy I transport very upset

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset turns the whole string upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Des, short for Desmond, a boy's name
a cart is a means of transport
so means very

explanation.surface: A boy left out after he wrecks his car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses DESICARTSO to give OS TRAC I SED.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or banish someone from a group is to shut them out.

clue.text: Streak of lightning over part of golf course

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means turned upside down, read backwards
a streak of the word is a thin run of its letters

explanation.surface: A bolt of lightning strikes the links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streak of' takes HTNIN from lightning; 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard golf course has eighteen holes, and this is the one ending the front half.

clue.text: Aware of having to follow voting system forthwith

indicators.note: the awareness phrase must come after the voting system

parts.note: PR is proportional representation
to be onto something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: Someone wise to an electoral scheme acts immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, without any delay; the answer is informal Spanish-derived slang.

clue.text: Bust of Caesar finally placed on support

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of Caesar

parts.note: aid is help or support

explanation.surface: A sculpted head of Caesar set on its plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the first piece is placed on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A police swoop on premises is slang for a bust or sudden search.

clue.text: PIN to disappear without right digital application

parts.note: to pin something is to nail it

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the vanishing word goes round the right

parts.note: to disappear is to vanish

explanation.surface: A bank PIN wiped out with no permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' means for the fingers, not computing.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish brushed on fingers is applied to the digits, a punning sense of digital.

clue.text: Outstanding bit of cricket shortened contest

parts.note: an over is six balls bowled in cricket

indicators.note: shortened means the contest word loses its last letter

parts.note: a duel is a contest

explanation.surface: A notable passage of cricket in a curtailed match.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still unpaid past its date is outstanding.

clue.text: Uncertain if I voted for this concoction of features

indicators.note: uncertain letters are unsettled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doubtful voter questioning a contrived face.
explanation.walkthrough: British police build a likeness of a suspect from witness memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A composite picture of a suspect's face is assembled on screen from separate facial elements.

clue.text: Quartet depart endless hosts to finally play for one

parts.note: to split is to leave, depart

indicators.note: the endless word plays host to the quartet, holding it inside

parts.note: endless means infinite
IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: A four-piece band breaks up, its endless hosting ending in one last performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: 'to finally play' puts an adverb between 'to' and the verb, the construction pedants object to.
explanation.definitionFit: Inserting an adverb between to and its verb is the grammatical construction named here, illustrated by the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Tatty article you left on sink

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means coming after the sinking word

parts.note: to sink a drink is to down it
A is the indefinite article
thee is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A shabby item someone abandoned on the kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby and run-down, like a shoe worn away at the back, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Drawing grains in brickwork, showing every imperfection

indicators.note: the drawing and grains go in the brickwork

parts.note: a wall is brickwork
drawing is art
sand is grains

explanation.surface: Sketching the sand grains within a brick wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from Cromwell's portrait request: depicted honestly, flaws included.

clue.text: Burning bible with papers

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Setting fire to a Bible along with documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning with enthusiasm means eager, keen to the point of passion.

clue.text: Jolly English judge participating in mass event

parts.note: a jolly is a pleasure trip

indicators.note: the English judge takes part inside the mass

parts.note: a lump is a mass

explanation.surface: A cheerful English judge joins a big crowd occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop, step and jump is a track-and-field contest in athletics.

clue.text: Rather like petrol alternative? One could give it a whirl!

definitions.text: One could give it a whirl!

parts.note: DERV is British diesel fuel for road vehicles
the suffix -ish means rather like

explanation.surface: A musing on diesel, then a cheerful suggestion to try it out.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British name for diesel road fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling member of a Sufi order spins in ecstatic dance, so literally gives it a whirl.

clue.text: Utterly unconvincing in speech days before Easter

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the words are heard not seen

parts.note: wholly weak means utterly unconvincing

explanation.surface: A feeble talk given just before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven days running up to Easter Sunday make the Christian holy period.

clue.text: Re offer, fabulous?

indicators.note: fabulous suggests something fanciful, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A comment on a sales pitch: what about this deal, isn't it great?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an offer costing nothing would be fabulous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given gratis, without charge, is the ideal offer the clue praises.

clue.text: Film director to take stock of soundtrack?

indicators.note: with a question mark, soundtrack hints at the sound of a word, so we hear rather than read it

parts.note: to rustle is to steal livestock, take stock

explanation.surface: A film director checking over a film's music.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Russell directed Women in Love and Tommy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Russell was an English filmmaker known for flamboyant features.

clue.text: Frenchman with directive put up extension

parts.note: René is a French man's name

indicators.note: in a down answer, put up reverses the word, reading upward

parts.note: a law is a directive

explanation.surface: A Frenchman builds an extension under official orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease or library loan is extended by being renewed.

clue.text: Happier having smallest coins in a line

indicators.note: the coins are placed in the line

parts.note: a tier is a row or line
1Ps, written IPS, are the smallest British coins

explanation.surface: Someone cheered by finding pennies all lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: 1p is the penny, smallest British coin; 1Ps is read as IPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy can mean merry with drink, so more tipsy is more happy in that sense.

clue.text: Pharaoh, from memory, repeated verse periodically

parts.note: RAM is computer memory

indicators.note: repeated means the picked letters appear twice
periodically takes every other letter of verse

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a pharaoh, reciting poetry over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Egyptian kings bore this name, notably the second, a famous ancient ruler.

clue.text: Joshua's father's sisters

definitions.meaning: in the Bible Joshua is the son of Nun, so belonging to Joshua's father

explanation.surface: A biblical aside about the aunts of Joshua.
explanation.definitionFit: Women in religious orders are called sisters; the Bible names Joshua as son of Nun.

clue.text: Match in Kew moved here?

indicators.note: moved signals the letters shifting into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A game at Kew relocated to this nearby place.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham, in south-west London a few miles from Kew Gardens, is England's national rugby stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby stadium near Kew is where an England international match would be played.

clue.text: Blackguard over the moon finding collector's item

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the scoundrel on top

parts.note: a cur is a scoundrel
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A rogue overjoyed to find an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the moon' looks like delight, but 'the moon' is Io.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare or unusual object prized by enthusiasts is a curiosity.

clue.text: Figure American's left standing

indicators.note: left as in departed, so the American goes out of the standing word

parts.note: standing means status
US, the United ...

explanation.surface: A figure the American left upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' looks like an upward reversal but it is the word to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for statistic, a numerical figure.

clue.text: Have bags of authority?

parts.note: bags are trousers in British slang, and the idiom is to be the one in charge of a household

explanation.surface: Wondering about someone with plenty of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old British slang for trousers, and 'bags of' also means lots of.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be the dominant partner who makes the decisions at home.

clue.text: Present that's not been opened before

indicators.note: unopened means losing the first letter

parts.note: present means here

explanation.surface: A gift still sealed, given earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic preposition meaning prior to.

clue.text: Disc behind something attached to vehicle

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A record lagging, then something fixed on a car.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver must show a red L on a white plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The learner's sign is fixed to the front and back of a car driven by a novice.

clue.text: Smoother variety of PE shorts

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means they appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An iron that suits all kinds of gym shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated pressing machine flattens paper or cloth, giving it a glossy finish.
